newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Shell Singapore begins crude run cuts by 2,000 TPD.
newsitem.headline: Shell Singapore begins crude run cuts by 2,000 TPD.

text.p: Shell Singapore has initiated a planned crude run cut on Tuesday to achieve an average June output of 57,000 tonne per day (TPD) from 59,000 TPD in the first half of June, sources close to the company said.
"The refinery is running at 57,000 TPD to day," the source said.
A Shell statement said on Monday that "During the month of June 1997, Shell Pukom refinery's production has to date, been running at around 59,000 TPD (430,000 barrel per day).
"As a response to market conditions, the plan is to achieve an average of 57,000 TPD for the month and this will entail production cuts in the second half of the month."
As a result, Shell is expected to extend its cuts further to 55,000 TPD to achieve the 57,000 TPD average target for the month.
The source said Shell might review this plan over the next two weeks if market conditions change considerably.

Shell has reduced its refinery output due to high stocks in Singapore which had forced some refiners to store their product at independent terminals and even sell distressed prompt cargoes at discounts of up to 40 cents below spot prices.
The high stocks are mainly middle distillates which after secondary processing amounts to up to 60 percent of a refinery's output.
Gas oil prices in Singapore have slumped to an 18-month low as a result of these high stocks, to trade at $22.20 per barrel free-on-board Singapore on Monday.
The lower price has also eaten into margins which have slipped to under 50 cents per barrel refined at the basic stage on Monday from about $1.00 late last week, traders said.
